rationale: One critical finding: missing test for the non-reset handleFilterChange path (spec partial, CR-001). Four major findings: Date.parse accepts locale-format dates bypassing ISO validation (CR-002); sanitizeUrlFilters drops time_period when only users/projects are valid and sends a temporally-unscoped API query (CR-003); resolveInitialFilters returns {} instead of DEFAULT_FILTERS when userId is null at mount (CR-004, reachability unconfirmed — cap at major); handleFilterChange's localStorage quota path leaves React state stale after a window.history.replaceState URL write, which useSearchParams does not observe (CR-005, reachability unconfirmed — cap at major). All five are introduced by this change's rewrite. Zero deferred, zero dismissed.

No dangerouslySetInnerHTML or innerHTML in changed files. clearUrlFilters builds newUrl from window.location parts and calls window.history.replaceState. No credentials logged; console.error calls log only error objects. No cross-window postMessage added. No nosonar markers introduced.

findings.title: Non-reset handleFilterChange path has no test
findings.problem: Spec requires a test calling handleFilterChange with a non-empty filter value (e.g., {time_period: 'last_7_days'}) and asserting setFilters is called with that value, but only the all-empty (isReset=true) path is exercised in the test suite.
findings.impact: The non-reset code path (lines 145–147 of useAnalyticsFilters.ts) handles every normal filter selection in production but is unverified; a regression in how non-empty filters propagate to setFilters would ship undetected.
findings.recommendation: Add a test case that invokes handleFilterChange({ time_period: TimePeriod.LAST_7_DAYS }) and asserts mockSetFilters was called with { time_period: TimePeriod.LAST_7_DAYS }, verifying the non-reset branch alongside the existing reset test.

findings.title: Date validator accepts non-ISO locale-format strings via Date.parse
findings.problem: isValidISODate uses Date.parse(v), which accepts locale-format strings such as 'Jan 1 2024' on most browsers; a URL param with a locale date passes the sanitization guard and is treated as a valid ISO date.
findings.impact: Non-ISO date strings reach the API in start_date/end_date fields; Date.parse behavior for locale strings is not standardized by ECMAScript, creating cross-browser inconsistency and potential silent data-range errors on the backend.
findings.recommendation: Replace the Date.parse check with an ISO 8601 prefix regex: /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}/.test(v) to ensure only well-formed ISO dates pass through sanitization.

findings.title: sanitizeUrlFilters omits time_period when only users/projects are valid
findings.problem: When the URL contains an invalid time_period alongside valid users or projects, sanitizeUrlFilters returns {users: [...]} without time_period; the fallback to DEFAULT_FILTERS only triggers when the result object is completely empty.
findings.impact: The API query is dispatched without temporal scope; depending on API defaults this may silently return data for an unexpected date range, and the behavior is non-deterministic across API versions.
findings.recommendation: After building the partial result, add: if (!result.time_period) result.time_period = DEFAULT_FILTERS.time_period; before the Object.keys length check, so temporal scope is always present in the sanitized output.

findings.title: Null userId at mount yields empty initial filters instead of DEFAULT_FILTERS
findings.problem: resolveInitialFilters returns {} when userId is null at mount; the useEffect guard prevents filter resolution, but child components receive a filters object with all fields undefined on first render.
findings.impact: Reachability unconfirmed: whether AnalyticsDashboard or any tab component fires an effect that dispatches an API call with time_period: undefined before userId resolves could not be established from the bounded read; if a downstream effect does fire, a request with no temporal scope is made.
findings.recommendation: Return DEFAULT_FILTERS instead of {} in resolveInitialFilters when userId is null, so all consumers always receive a well-formed filter set regardless of auth hydration state.

findings.title: localStorage quota error leaves React state stale after URL write
findings.problem: handleFilterChange calls setFilters (which writes the URL via window.history.replaceState before writing localStorage) then setFilterState; if localStorage throws a quota error, the catch block silences the exception before setFilterState runs, leaving React state at the old filter values while the URL holds new ones.
findings.impact: Reachability unconfirmed (localStorage quota exceeded is low-probability); when it occurs, UI filter controls display stale values until the next navigation event. Because setFilters uses window.history.replaceState rather than React Router navigation, useSearchParams does not observe the URL change and the reactive useEffect that would re-sync state does not fire.
findings.recommendation: Move setFilterState(filtersToApply) before the setFilters call, or place it in a finally block, so React state is updated regardless of whether the localStorage write succeeds.
